newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar late on Wednesday on high liquidity and worries over the coming election campaign, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said reports of a strike by some 10,000 workers under contract to Nike Inc and flush rupiah supply in the afternoon boosted sentiment on the U.S. currency.

Some 10,000 of the 13,000 workers at a factory under contract to Nike marched from their plant in Tangerang on Jakarta's outskirts to the local parliament on Tuesday to demand a wage increase. They were granted a pay rise after staging a mass strike and protest, Antara news agency reported.
"The tone is still biddish on the dollar. But there is a lot of fight at the 2,420 level," the dealer said.

Dealers said ample rupiah liquidity also helped dollar purchasing. One local bank dealer expected more upside for the dollar after it broke through the 2,420 resistance level several times. Spot rupiah was at 2,420.00/20.25 at 0930 GMT after fluctuating between the 2,417.0 and 2,421.0 range.

One currency dealer in Singapore said the tone seemed to be biddish on the dollar, with the brief response to the Nike demonstration reflecting only general caution ahead of the campaign starting on Sunday for the May 29 elections.

The rupiah strengthened briefly in the morning following a report in a local daily quoting a university professor and an unnamed official as saying the central bank was planning a band widening in the near future. But the report was later ignored by the market as operators switched focus to politics.
A noted economist said the central bank was unlikely to widen its band in the short- or medium-term because there was no fundamental reason to back it up at present.
"The rate is hovering at a healthy level below the mid-rate of the intervention band and moderately higher than the floor rate. I don't see any reason to act now," the economist said.
He said the central bank had implemented a new reserve rate of five percent only last Wednesday which should help contain money supply growth, which exceeded targets in 1996.
The economist said there was no immediate reason to act and the effect of the new reserve rate had to be disgested first.
"Political issues are taking the lead for now. People are worried over possible riots and things like that as we enter the campaign period," the Singapore dealer said.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,419.40/19.80 and 2,416.5/17.0, respectively.
Overnight money fell to 9.5 percent in the afternoon from 13.0 percent. Overnight swaps were at 0.45/0.50 points.
Dealers said swap premiums were little changed from the opening after fluctuating in narrow-range trading.
They said the focus was on the spot market.
One-month swaps were at 11.5/12.5, two at 23.0/23.5, three at 33.75/34.75 and six at 71.5/72.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,404/2,596 and the conversion band at 2,404/2,452 on Wednesday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
